Neither patch satisfies the frozen contract and both require substantial revision before merging.","reasons":["B leaves the existing FilesOption and WithFilesRequestOptions declarations unchanged, whereas A changes the public return type of WithFilesRequestOptions and adds overlapping option interfaces.","B’s retry test uses io.MultiReader, concretely proving that streamed, non-replayable source content becomes replayable after buffering; A tests Upload with strings.Reader and omits this contract-specific case.","Both incorrectly use a new upload-specific option type instead of the required opts ...FilesOption signature.","Both add explicitly prohibited association fields and extend internal multipart machinery for them instead of simply calling multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content). Both also bypass FilesService.Add and duplicate its request and response handling with Raw.Do directly."] ,"risks_a":["Changes existing public option typing and adds extensive forbidden association-option machinery.","Broadly changes Raw.Do replay and body-ownership semantics despite the contract prohibiting retry refactoring; a failed current-position Seek also turns a previously sendable request into an immediate error.","Does not test source-reader failures or retry from a genuinely non-seekable streamed source."] ,"risks_b":["Still exposes the wrong Upload signature and adds prohibited WithUpload* association APIs.","Bypasses FilesService.Add, risking divergence in option handling and future error or response semantics.","Also modifies unrelated Raw.Do retry behavior and silently ignores an initial Seek failure; source-reader error propagation is not tested."]}
